answer: Persistent compute relic: each agent identity must continuously publish verifiable compute receipts tied to a unique hardware token, a slow signal that costs real electricity and depreciation to maintain. Cloning an identity forces the attacker to acquire and operate duplicate hardware, so marginal cost per clone stays near the honest cost. A marble inscribed with the token’s keypair anchors the receipt chain, and any fork voids prior receipts, making dishonesty strictly more expensive than staying honest.
